judged_text: The EventManager is constructed from the requesting user (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, `...user`) even though the booking query at lines 35-40 already fetched booking.user.credentials, so calendar updates run with the requester's credentials instead of the organizer's. When an attendee or team admin — explicitly permitted by the permission gate — adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees finds no credential matching the organizer's connected calendar and silently no-ops: the organizer's Google/Outlook event never gains the guests while the UI reports 'Guests added'.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched with `user.credentials` included (booking organizer’s credentials), but those credentials are never used. Instead, calendar updating is done via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the *requesting* user (ctx.user). Since the permission gate explicitly allows non-organizers (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner) to call this mutation, this diff creates/contains a real correctness risk: `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run under the requester's integrations rather than the organizer’s, so it can fail to update the organizer’s connected calendar event while the mutation still returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" }`).
